quote: Forgiving, in other words, is the only reaction which does not merely re-act but acts anew and unexpectedly, unconditioned by the act which provoked it and therefore freeing from its consequences both the one who forgives and the one who is forgiven.
source: Hannah Arendt, The Human Condition, chapter V, section 33, Irreversibility and the Power to Forgive (Chicago, 1958), p. 241

evidence.where: Section 33 of The Human Condition as reproduced in full on the What Is Compelling blog and excerpted at The Marginalian and Plough, checked against the University of Chicago Press text (1958; the 1998 second edition keeps the pagination)
evidence.edition: The Human Condition, University of Chicago Press, 1958
evidence.locator: Chapter V (Action), section 33, Irreversibility and the Power to Forgive, p. 241

reason: The sentence is Arendt's own English, word for word as printed in section 33, and it is the sentence the forgiveness argument of the book is known by. Not shipped anywhere; Arendt stands at one of three for the year (month 1), so a second line in month 2 is allowed; not banned.
